rationale: A Pulp UI can display a parameter, because a parameter has a name it can ask for, but it cannot display gain reduction, an envelope follower's output, or a detector's state, because those live inside process() and are nameless. Authors hand-roll a TripleBuffer and a bespoke binding per plugin, so most plugins ship a UI that cannot show what the plugin is doing. This adds the primitives for named channels a UI resolves by name. One transferred surface moves with it: value_source.hpp gains VectorFrame and VectorSource alongside the existing MeterSource and ScalarSource, following the same fixed-capacity-plus-runtime-count shape MeterFrame already uses so the payload stays trivially copyable and rides the existing TripleBuffer with no new lock-free code. Nothing existing changes: MeterFrame, MeterSource and ScalarSource are untouched, and the addition is additive at the end of the header. The registry itself (value_channel_set.hpp/.cpp) is new and outside the transferred slice. This is Pulp-specific plugin-UI capability work with no counterpart framework behaviour to backport.
